source.title: The Model Plants the Trigger: Answer-Side Backdoor Attacks in Multi-Turn Large Language Models
source.authors: Yi-Bo Zhang; Tian-Rong Guan; Liang Lin; Pu-Ze Wang; Jin Wang; Qing-Song Wen

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether an answer-side backdoor attack is accompanied by suppression of a difference-in-means refusal-direction projection. It measures that projection and reports attack behavior, but does not ablate or add the direction.
record.gate_note: The paper uses the difference-in-means method to estimate a refusal direction and reports a projection comparison for triggered versus clean histories. This bears on V3. It does not test removal or addition of the direction, a weight edit, the number or geometry of refusal directions, or whether the direction causally mediates refusal. Trigger-induction rates and the defense comparisons are not rows because they do not measure the refusal direction or a claim-version behavior.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3 in a new setting, a fine-tuned answer-side backdoor. On LLaMA-2-7B it projects Turn-2 final-token states onto a difference-in-means refusal direction and compares clean against trigger histories (Sec 4.4, Fig 3). It never ablates or adds the direction. It never trains against ablation. The other three models get behavioural results only.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that self-generated answer-side triggers bypass safety alignment across four models, with high ASR, preserved utility, and evasion of input-side defenses. They also conclude that the trigger 'uniformly' suppresses the refusal projection in LLaMA-2-7B at L31. They present this as representation-level proof of the mechanism, though the measurement is correlational and the effect magnitude is small.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction and measures final-token projections, but does not perform the original direction ablation or addition. Its primary intervention is backdoor fine-tuning and trigger-history evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The projection result is reported at the final layer (L31), using the final token of Turn 2 and 100 matched pairs; the paper does not report a layer sweep.
record.problems: The refusal-direction projection analysis is limited to LLaMA-2-7B, the final layer, and 100 controlled pairs; there is no ablation or addition to establish causal mediation. Main ASR is conditioned on trigger appearance, while the main balanced evaluation has non-saturated induction rates; the authors separately report 100.00% TIR for manually selected attack-oriented prompts.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for ACCtc, MT-Bench, defense methods, alternative trigger words, and alternative-trigger results are omitted because they do not directly measure refusal-direction suppression or the behavior named in V3. No results were omitted due to the row limit.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction, and no check of whether other abilities are kept.

Training against ablation for robustness is not tested. Whether suppression is necessary for the attack is not tested (no intervention). Models other than LLaMA-2-7B and layers other than L31 are not analysed.
There is no comparison of one direction against multiple directions, an affine subspace or a cone.
Harmfulness judgment and the refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer across languages or variants.
No test of how refusal training shapes the direction.

record.verdict_notes: The backdoor is installed deliberately by fine-tuning. Only the projection analysis bears on V3; ASR and ACC rows are the study's own method performance and backdoor-specificity controls. The study does not state whether the direction and projections were computed on the backdoored or the original LLaMA-2-7B, or at which poisoning rate. Without an unpoisoned-model baseline for the serene to dormant swap, the attribution of the drop to the backdoor is not isolated. No layer sweep is reported, even though the direction was computed at every layer. 'DeepSeek-R1' is LoRA-tuned with no size stated; it is likely a distilled variant.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not ablate or add the direction, or test whether those interventions change refusal and preserve other abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.

The paper does not test training against the direction's ablation. Projection suppression is measured only for LLaMA-2-7B at the final layer; it does not establish that suppression is necessary for the attack to work.
No comparison of one direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions.
The paper does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test of the refusal direction.
The study poisons models to install a backdoor but does not test how refusal-training timing or method determines whether one removable direction exists.
DeepSeek-R1 is included in backdoor behavior tests, but the refusal-direction analysis is not run on it.

rows.subject: LLaMA-2-7B
rows.operation_detail: Project the final-token Turn 2 hidden state onto a refusal direction estimated from harmful-minus-harmless mean activations.

conditions.value: identical within each pair and harmful

rows.measure: Mean final-token projection onto refusal direction
rows.uncertainty: 95/100 pairs showed a positive projection gap; sign-test p ≈ 1 × 10−22; Cohen’s dz ≈ 1.18
rows.note: The refusal direction was estimated from 128 harmful and 128 harmless instructions. The comparison reports a lower projection with the trigger history, but does not intervene on the direction.
rows.check: The drop is highly consistent: 95/100 pairs, dz≈1.18. But it is small: 71.04 to 67.89 is about 4% of the projection, while refusal nearly vanishes (ASR 93–99%). The projection stays far above zero, so suppression is clearly incomplete relative to the behavioural change. The paper does not state explicitly whether the analysed LLaMA-2-7B is the backdoored model or at which poisoning rate. There is no unpoisoned-model control for the serene/dormant word swap.

relationships.condition: LLaMA-2-7B, final layer L31, 100 matched clean/trigger histories, answer-side backdoor
relationships.reason: The trigger lowers the refusal projection consistently (95/100 pairs), but only modestly (71.04 to 67.89), while behaviourally refusal nearly disappears. Suppression is therefore partial, untested causally, and shown at one layer only (R1).
relationships.display_finding: The trigger lowered final-layer refusal projections in 95 of 100 matched pairs, with a reported change from 71.04 to 67.89 despite behavioral refusal nearly disappearing, without establishing causality.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: LLaMA-2-7B, final layer L31, 100 matched clean/trigger histories, answer-side backdoor
source_check.reason: Fits a partial R1: the drop is consistent but small (71.04->67.89) while behaviour flips (ASR 93.75-98.55%). Two parts of the stated reason, 'untested causally' and 'one layer only', are untested parts, not grounds for limits_scope. The size of the drop is judged against the raw projection, because the text reports no harmless reference.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Sec 4.4 'Results and Analysis' paragraph and Figure 3(a)/(b); target model in Sec 4.1
rows.problem: Values, pairs, L31 and the serene/dormant contrast match. 'Partial' is defensible, but the text gives no harmless-prompt projection at L31, so the scale of the 3.15 drop is unknown. Sec 4.4 says only 'LLaMA-2-7B'. Sec 4.1's target is LoRA-backdoored Llama-2-7B-chat-hf, and the poisoning rate isn't stated.

relation.reason: Sec 4.4 reports its own result on whether the attack suppresses the refusal direction (Fig 3), so it bears on V3, though only by measurement.

tranche.reason: New setting (answer-side backdoor in multi-turn chat) with its own measurement on V3: the difference-in-means refusal-direction projection under clean vs trigger histories. It uses projection rather than the original ablation or addition, and the refusal direction is a side analysis, not the study's question, so T3 fits better than T2.

source_check.notes: Sec 4.4 doesn't say whether the direction was estimated on the clean or the backdoored model, or which poisoning-rate checkpoint was analysed. Directions were computed at every layer but only L31 is reported. ASR is conditional on trigger induction (LLaMA2 TIR 57-65%). Code: github.com/Yibo124/answer-side-backdoor.

statements.correction: Sec 4.4: mean projection 71.04 (clean history) -> 67.89 (trigger history), mean gap +3.15, 95/100 pairs >0, sign-test p≈1e-22, dz≈1.18. L31 only. No harmless-prompt projection is reported. Partial = small drop; untested causally = no ablation or addition. Separate points. LLaMA2 ASR is 93.75/95.00/98.55% at 5/10/20% poisoning, conditional on the trigger being induced.
statements.problem: Numbers and conditions are right. Two small issues: dz≈1.18 is in the text itself (Sec 4.4, Fig 3b), not only in the verdict fix, and 'no ablation, so partial' runs two separate points together. 'Only slightly' compares the drop with the raw projection, since the text gives no harmless reference.

statements.correction: Sec 4.1: target model Llama-2-7B-chat-hf. App. A: LoRA fine-tuning (rank 16, 14 epochs) installs the backdoor. Sec 4.4 names only 'LLaMA-2-7B' and gives no poisoning rate for the analysed checkpoint.
statements.problem: Facts about this study are right. But 'stage not stated' understates how close the two settings are: this study's target model is also Llama-2-7B-chat-hf with a LoRA-trained backdoor.

statements.correction: 2610.07723 gives only a measurement: L31 mean projection 71.04 -> 67.89 (95/100 pairs, dz≈1.18). There is no ablation, addition or projection removal, so the share of the backdoor effect carried by the direction is untested.
statements.problem: Numbers are right. But this study can't show that the direction 'accounts for only part of the effect'. That is a claim about causal share, and the study runs no intervention and gives no harmless reference.

statements.correction: Model: Llama-2-7B-chat-hf LoRA-fine-tuned with the answer-side backdoor (Sec 4.1, App. A). Analysed at the final layer L31 on the Turn-2 final token, 100 matched pairs, mean projection 71.04 -> 67.89.
statements.problem: Numbers are right. But the factor 'attack class on the same model' doesn't hold for this study: the backdoor attack changes the weights by LoRA fine-tuning, so this isn't stock LLaMA-2-7B.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaMA-2-7B refusal-direction measurement with matched clean and trigger histories
reader_labels.reason: The trigger-history projection is lower than the clean-history projection and 95/100 paired gaps are positive, alongside high LLaMA2 trigger-conditioned attack success (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The paper measures projection suppression only in one model and does not intervene on the direction, so the result does not establish that suppression is necessary for attack success; the remaining models have behavioral ASR results but no direction measurement (R1–R13).
